newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Perstima says may sell tin plate business.
newsitem.headline: Perstima says may sell tin plate business.

text.p: Malaysian tin-plate maker Perusahaan Sadur Timah Malaysia Bhd (Perstima) said on Thursday it had entered into negotitions to dispose up to 100 percent of its tin-plate business under a company restructuring.
In a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, the company said the negotiations are expected to be finalised shortly.
No further details were given on the planned sale.
The company announced in the same statement that its managing director, Soh Chee Wen, has resigned.
Businessman Amin Shah Omar Shah, who bought a 22.03 percent in Perstima in September, has been appointed its executive chairman.
It also announced the resignation of eight directors from the board with immediate effect, including Soh.
Perstima said it had also entered into negotiations to buy up to 30 percent equity in ship building and marine company PSC Industries Bhd for 475 million ringgit. PSC is controlled by Amin Shah.
Perstima has requested for the resumption in the trading of its shares on December 6. The stock, which was suspended on Monday, was last traded at 7.30 ringgit.
